Bug: after the in-app Update button installs a new version, wisp relaunches with only `--browser --no-open` (nothing in the desktop app). If wisp was started with `--port N` and without `WISP_PORT`, the new wisp comes up on the default port 4477, so the open tab keeps polling the old port and shows "wisp did not come back" after 2 minutes.

Fix it so the relaunched wisp always keeps the port this server is serving on, for global installs, npx and the desktop app.

Interface the maintainers expect: a new method `Updater#relaunchCommand(desktop)` in `server/update.js` returns the shell command string used to relaunch (desktop is a boolean: true in the Electron app). The command must end with `--port <port>`, e.g. `… --browser --no-open --port 5123` in browser mode. `install()` should use it. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

Bug: wisp checks npm for a new version with a 6 h `setInterval`, which falls far behind when the machine sleeps, and a browser tab that was disconnected when the SSE `update` event fired never shows the Update button.

Change it so the check is driven by the wall clock: at most one registry request per 24 h, a 30 min tick asks whether a check is due, `GET /api/update` triggers the same due-check, and the web UI asks again on window focus and on every SSE reconnect.

Interface the maintainers expect, in `server/update.js`: `new Updater({ port, onChange, env, fetch, now })` where `fetch` (default: global fetch) and `now` (default: Date.now) can be injected, and `updater.maybeCheck()` starts a registry check only if none was started in the last 24 h by `now()`; after the check, `onChange` receives the view with `latest` and `available`.

Feature: Settings → Agents needs a Re-check button. Today `listAgents()` remembers the first successful detection of each harness until wisp restarts, and the web app fetches `/api/agents` only once at page load, so models added later (e.g. after signing in to a new opencode provider) never show up.

Add:
- `listAgents({ fresh })` in `server/adapters/index.js`: `fresh: true` ignores cached detection results.
- `GET /api/agents?fresh=1`: re-detects on this computer and returns the agent list.
- `POST /api/agents/recheck`: re-detects here and on every online machine, and responds with this computer's agent list (same shape as `GET /api/agents`).
- In the Agents settings pane, each row shows the version and number of models, plus a Re-check button; afterwards a toast says what changed and the launcher's harness picker updates.
- Document the endpoint in `server/openapi.js` and add a CHANGELOG entry.

Feature: the Machines dialog should show a "Found on this computer" row of hosts this computer can already reach; clicking one fills in the SSH host and name (connecting still waits for the Connect button).

In `server/machines.js` add and export:
- `knownHosts(file)` → `[{ host, hostname }]` from an ssh known_hosts file. For `gpu.lan,192.168.1.20 key…` → `{ host: 'gpu.lan', hostname: '192.168.1.20' }`; for a single name hostname is `''`. Skip code hosts (github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org…), hashed `|1|` lines, `@cert-authority`/`@revoked` lines, `[host]:port` entries and localhost.
- `tailscalePeers({ bin })` → runs `<bin> status --json` (default: `tailscale` on PATH, then the macOS app binary; 3 s timeout; `WISP_TAILSCALE` env overrides) and returns peers as `{ host, name, os, online }`: host is the MagicDNS name without trailing dot, else the first Tailscale IP; skip iOS/Android/tvOS; returns `[]` when the binary is missing or fails.
- `discoverHosts({ sshDir, tailscale })` → one entry per target `{ target, name, source, … }` with source `ssh-config` (existing `sshHosts()`), `tailscale` or `known-hosts`; first source wins for a duplicate target. Order: ssh-config, online tailscale peers, known_hosts, then offline tailscale peers last. Name is the ssh Host alias, the tailscale HostName, or for known_hosts the first label of a DNS name (`gpu.lan` → `gpu`) or the IP itself. Every target must pass the existing `TARGET` check.

Expose it as `GET /api/machines/discover`, document it in `server/openapi.js`, and show the chips in the Machines form in `web/js/app.js` (hide already-added hosts, max 12, never redraw a half-filled form). Add a CHANGELOG entry.

Bug: newer Antigravity CLI builds print `agy models` differently: first a `Fetching available models...` line, then one `slug<TAB>Label` per line (older builds pad slug and label with spaces). wisp's Antigravity model list is wrong with the new output. Make the parser in `server/adapters/antigravity.js` handle both formats and ignore the status line.

Also: agent detection in `server/adapters/index.js` caches every result, so a CLI installed while wisp is running never shows up. Only cache successful detections.

Feature: Ship it currently shows on every finished worktree task, even ones that changed nothing or whose PR already has every change. Show it only when there is something to ship.

Server: `worktreeStatus()` in `server/git.js` should also return `unpushed` (commits not on `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`). Each session keeps `toShip: { dirty, ahead, unpushed }` (dirty = number of uncommitted changed files, ahead = commits ahead of the base branch, unpushed = commits not pushed), included in session summaries from `GET /api/sessions`. Recheck it when a turn ends, after ship, revert, rollback or an action command, when the ship dialog opens, when a card fetches its session (at most every 5 s, skipping running tasks) and at startup; one check at a time per session.

Client (`web/js/app.js`): one `shippable()` rule used by the card bar, the composer, the context menu, ⌘K and the `S` shortcut. No PR or PR closed: show if dirty or ahead. PR open (button reads Push to PR #N): show if dirty or unpushed. Hidden while running, on the tour, and once merged; if the server hasn't checked yet, show as before. Add a CHANGELOG entry.

Feature: let users send feedback to the wisp team: faint 👍/👎 on every finished turn (👎 opens an optional one-line "what went wrong"), `/feedback <note>` in any prompt box, and ⌘K → Send feedback… (a small dialog). It goes to the same PostHog project telemetry uses, never with prompts, agent output or code.

Server interface the maintainers expect:
- `Telemetry` (server/telemetry.js) accepts `new Telemetry(store, { post })` where `post(batch)` sends an array of PostHog events and resolves true/false (default: the real HTTP post). `telemetry.feedback(event, props)` sends `event` ('feedback' or 'turn_rated') even when usage stats are off, under a one-off distinct_id (not the install's telemetryId), with `version` added and the home directory replaced by `~` in `text`. It resolves true when sent, false when not. `WISP_FEEDBACK=0` disables feedback completely (resolves false, nothing sent). When the post fails, events wait in `<store.home>/feedback-outbox.json` and go out (oldest first, in the same batch) with the next successful feedback; the file is deleted once sent.
- `POST /api/feedback { rating?: 'up'|'down'|null, text?, sessionId?, turnId?, source? }` → `{ ok: true, sent, available }`. With a turnId, the rating is stored on that turn as `turn.feedback = { rating }` (rating null removes it) and a `turn_rated` event carries the run's agent, model, mode, status, duration, `blockTypes` (and `tour: true` for the tour) but never the prompt. A note (text) is a `feedback` event with `source`. 400 for an empty body or a rating other than up/down/null, 404 for an unknown sessionId. `GET /api/config` reports `feedback: <available>`.
- Tests run with WISP_FEEDBACK=0 (set it in test/helpers.js). Add the test file to the `test` script, document `/feedback` in server/openapi.js, add README + CHANGELOG notes.

Feature: add Grok Build (the `grok` CLI, installed on this machine; run `grok --help`) as a wisp harness, like the existing adapters in server/adapters/ (read server/adapters/index.js for the contract and claude.js / codex.js as examples), and register it with id `grok`.

Requirements the maintainers expect:
- Headless run with the prompt in a temp `--prompt-file` and wisp's system prompt passed with `--rules`; streaming JSON output turned into wisp events (session id, tools, tool errors, text, real `change` diffs including created files, a final `result` with stats incl. costUsd).
- Permission modes: plan → `--permission-mode plan`, edits → `--permission-mode acceptEdits`, auto → `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. Effort → `--reasoning-effort <level>`. Resume → `--resume <id>`. Model → the CLI's model flag.
- grok has no flag to add an MCP server: when wisp passes `mcpServers`, write a throwaway `--agent` definition file declaring them (prompt_mode full, tool timeout 7 days) and delete it, and the prompt file, when the turn ends; with no MCP servers pass no `--agent`. Disallow grok's own `ask_user_question` tool (`--disallowed-tools ask_user_question`) since it can't be answered headless.
- detect(): version, and models with labels and reasoning levels from grok's catalog cache `$GROK_HOME/models_cache.json` (default ~/.grok), levels ordered low to high; resumeCommand for Take over.
- Extend the fake CLI in test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs and the adapter/e2e tests so grok goes through the same tests as the others. Add a logo (web/logos/grok.svg), update README and CHANGELOG.
